DEFAULT_RUNTIME.title: Default pump runtime when the user hasn't entered one

value.reason: At 8 h/day a salt cell sized by the 2x rule usually needs more than the 50% scale-control limit (e.g. 87% for 20k gal hot & sunny); at 12 h typical pools land at about 30-45%, matching TFP's run-longer-at-low-speed advice, for roughly $18/yr more pump energy on a 20k pool. Users can edit it; PoolMath can pre-fill the user's real schedule.

TURNOVER_FORMULA.title: Minimum flow is set by equipment, not pool volume

value.skimmerNote: A single skimmer works properly down to about 15 GPM on most designs.
value.formula: minimumGPM = max(skimmer 15, SWG flow switch if fitted (SWG_FLOW_SWITCH.byTee)); the gas heater minimum is a peak demand (FEATURE_FLOW_DEMANDS) unless heaterSetsDailyMinimum
value.supersedes: poolGallons / 8 turnover. Turnover does not determine minimum flow for a residential pool.
value.commercialCaveat: Commercial pools DO have firm turnover requirements. This tool is residential-only.
value.changeReason: 2026-11 (pending review): the SWG threshold was 22 GPM here but 25 GPM in SWG_FLOW_SWITCH, so the engine could say a pump 'idles down to 22 GPM' and then warn it needs 25. Unified on SWG_FLOW_SWITCH. The gas heater only needs ~40 GPM while firing (the heater-bypass rule notes it is idle ~95% of the time), so forcing 40 GPM all day overstated running cost by several times for every pool with a heater.

SWG_FLOW_SWITCH.title: Salt cell flow switch trips on velocity, not flow

value.note: The flow switch is activated by water velocity, so the tee size sets the threshold. A 2″ tee needs about 25 GPM; swapping to a 1.5″ tee drops it to about 14 GPM. Use the tee supplied with the cell.
value.risk: A variable-speed pump run too slowly will not close the switch, and the cell silently stops making chlorine.

CELL_LIFE.title: Salt cell life and why oversizing pays

value.note: Manufacturer ratings assume the pump runs 24/7 with the cell generating continuously. Oversizing lets you run shorter pump times at a lower output percentage, which extends cell life.
value.warrantyCaution: Be wary of long prorated warranties on generic cells — the proration basis is often undisclosed.

CELL_LIFE.src: TFP wiki: Hayward AquaRite SWG — cell life / generic cells

AQUARITE_CELL_TYPE.title: AquaRite infers salinity from the cell — the T-Cell type setting must match

value.fact: Hayward AquaRite (and clones such as CircuPool RJ) have no separate salt sensor; they infer salinity from cell performance. If the T-Cell type setting does not match the installed cell, salt reads wrong — a larger cell than the setting reads high, a smaller one reads low.
value.risk: A wrong reading can trip a low-salt / check-cell warning, which shuts off chlorine production.
value.alsoTrips: Low salt, a dirty or scaled cell, trapped air, or cold water can trip the same warning.
value.verify: TFP recommends confirming actual salt with a Taylor K-1766 (or TF Salt) drop test rather than trusting the panel.

AQUARITE_CELL_TYPE.src: TFP: SWG chemistry — how salt systems determine salinity

SWG_CYA_CELL_LIFE.title: CYA 70-80 makes the cell work less hard

value.why: Higher CYA shields chlorine from UV, so the cell produces less to hold the same FC — which extends cell life.
value.percentIsRuntime: The output percentage is a fraction of pump run time, so changing your pump schedule changes chlorine output and the percentage needs re-tuning.

SWG_CYA_CELL_LIFE.src: TFP: SWG chemistry — water balance targets

SWG_ONOFF_ONLY.title: Some cells have no percentage adjustment

value.fact: Intex salt systems run at 100% or off — there is no output percentage, so chlorine output is controlled purely by pump run time.

reasons: Isolate a leaking or failed heater without shutting the pump down, so the pool keeps circulating and chlorinating.
Protect the copper heat exchanger when pH drops below about 7.0 — acidic water erodes the core and can stain the pool.
Cut back pressure for the ~95% of the time the heater is not in use; heat pumps restrict more than gas heaters because of smaller internal piping.
value.note: An internal bypass or a flow-limiting external bypass is not the same thing — neither can stop water flowing through the core.

PUMP_ENERGY_MODEL.title: How daily pump energy is estimated

value.formula: VS: watts(Q) = fixed + k*Q^3, fitted through the CEC low- and high-speed points on the chosen curve; capped at high-speed watts. Two-/multi-speed: low-speed watts if low speed delivers the daily minimum, else high-speed watts. Single-speed: high-speed watts.
value.changeReason: Pure cube-law scaling from the low point ignores the drive/motor losses that stay roughly constant at low speed (median ~40 W in the CEC data), so pumps tested at a higher low-speed flow looked unrealistically cheap at 15-25 GPM and before/after comparisons could show negative savings. Two-/multi-speed pumps were also modelled as if they could throttle like a VS, understating their running cost.

PUMP_ENERGY_MODEL.src: Pump affinity laws on a fixed system curve; CEC appliance database test points
